Best score 10/36 (99.7%). Function logic is correct. Remaining diff is 2 regalloc instructions in the else branch: target does `ldrb r1,[r2]; movs r0,#0x40; orrs r0,r1; strb r0,[r2]` (r2 = arg0+0x2A), mine does `ldrb r0,[r2]; movs r1,#0x40; orrs r0,r1; strb r0,[r2]`. Tried: declaration order (flags/q/p/r, q/p/flags/r, p first, a/b locals, u8 v local, array indexing arg0[0x2A], `0x40 | *p` vs `*p |= 0x40`, `0xBF & *p` vs `*p &= 0xBF`). The working best form: r computed first, then if(r==1){p=arg0+0x2A; *p=0xBF&*p; q=arg1+0x28; if(q) q[1]=0; if(!(0xD&*(u16*)arg1)) return 1; return 0;} p=arg0+0x2A; *p|=0x40; return 0. The regalloc difference is stubborn — likely needs the two arg0+0x2A stores to share a temp differently, or the `flags` load scheduled after the q check. Next agent: try computing `*(u8*)(arg0+0x2A)` into a named u8 local used for both branches, or reorder so the else-branch load happens before the q/flags block.

Best score 60/97: compiler pins r0 to the hash accumulator rather than r3. Tried u32 vs int locals, declaration order, extra temporaries, re-associating the XOR: all no effect. Remaining diff is register allocation only (target keeps r0 as the running accumulator). No C shape change moves it.

Best score 315/28 insns (88.7%). Logic is correct and verified against assembly: arg0+0x3C holds a pointer to a struct whose first u16 is a flag word; if pointer NULL or arg1 NULL return; if (flags & 0x20) return; if ((flags & 3) || (*(u16*)(arg1+0x14) & 1)) { set flags |= 0x20; call sub_08062394(0, *(u8*)(ptr+0x1C)); }. Remaining diff is pure register allocation: original uses push {lr} only and keeps the pointer in r3 and the u16 value in r2 (computing `0x20 | v` into r0 via movs r0,#0x20; orrs r0,r2); my C makes agbcc spill to r4 (push {r4,lr}) and emit an extra `adds r3,r2,#0`. Tried: u8*/u16*/struct-typed pointer locals, early-return vs nested-if, `& 0xC` vs `!= 0`, value cached in a local — no change to score. Suspect the fix is local declaration order / variable lifetime so agbcc keeps the pointer in r3 and the u16 in r2 with no callee-saved register. Also note: compile_and_diff warns "you call sub_08062394 where the original calls something else" but the project's own call graph lists sub_080142C0 under sub_08062394's called-by, so treat that note as a signature artifact. sub_08062394's real signature is (u8, u8) per its own assembly (lsls/lsrs #18 truncation on both args).

Best score 215/9 insns (76.1%). Logic: if (*arg0 & 0xC) then *(u8*)(arg1+1) = 0. Target has no push/pop (leaf, 9 insns); mine emits push {lr}/pop {r0} (11 insns) because agbcc thinks the function needs a frame. Tried every variant: u16*/u8*/struct-typed arg1, `& 0xC` vs `!= 0`, caching *arg0 in a local, static, non-inline, inlined-style. search_flags tried -O1/-O2/-O3/-Os/-fno-strength-reduce: project's -O2 is best, so it's not flags. The extra instructions are push {lr}, pop {r0} and a 2-byte branch offset difference (beq #0x10 vs #0x12). Likely cause: the original was compiled as a leaf with arg1 typed so the +1 store needs no address materialization, or the function is declared with a prototype that lets agbcc skip the frame. Caller sub_08033BCC passes (r4 = arg0+0x3C, r7 = arg0+0x48) then `ldr r1,[r7,#0xC]` so arg1 is a pointer+0xC. Next agent: try declaring arg1 as a struct pointer with the byte at offset 1, try __attribute__((naked)) alternatives, or try compiling with the agbcc-own-b3673d20 compiler.

Best score 1750/37 insns (52.7%). Logic verified: arg0+0x30 is a linked-list head; walk it setting each node's +0x28 to *(void**)(D_02025FF0+0x1870); then take g = *(void**)(D_02025FF0+0x1870); g = g->+0x30; if g non-null walk to tail via +0x2C, set tail->+0x2C = old head, set arg0->+0x30 = NULL. Remaining diff is register allocation + literal pool layout: original emits two separate literals (ldr r2,[pc,#0x28]=0x02025FF0, ldr r4,[pc,#0x2c]=0x1870) then `adds r0,r2,r4`, i.e. it does NOT fold &D_02025FF0+0x1870 into one literal — agbcc folds it for me. Tried: extern vu32/vu8/char/u8[]/struct{u8 pad[0x1870]; void*} D_02025FF0, local u8* base pointer, bare 0x02025FF0 numeric — the array/char/vu8 forms keep the two-literal shape (best 1750) but agbcc still folds; the struct form (2026) and local pointer (1986) are worse. The blocker is that agbcc's address-folding merges the base and offset into one literal; the original was compiled without that folding, or with a symbol that inhibits it. Next agent: try declaring D_02025FF0 as `extern volatile u32 D_02025FF0[]` combined with taking its address via a helper, or try the agbcc-own-b3673d20 compiler via try_compiler, or mark the function NONMATCHING and hand the literal-pool problem to the user.

First 23 of 34 instructions match exactly. Remaining diff is only literal-pool placement + 2 trailing `movs r0,r0` padding: target emits `ldr r2,[pc,#0x14]` then `ldr r3,[r2]` (literal 0x08671BD0 placed at the function end, 34 insns, no trailing padding); mine emits `ldr r2,[pc,#0xc]` then `ldr r3,[r2]` plus 2 extra `movs r0,r0` (36 insns). Tried: u32 v local vs direct *(u32*)0x08671BD0 vs extern u32 D_08671BD0 vs extern u32*const — the direct `*(u32*)0x08671BD0` form is best (400). The 2 extra movs appear to be agbcc's alignment padding that the target's code shape avoids. Next agent: try declaring the constant as `extern const u32 D_08671BD0;` and passing `D_08671BD0`, or restructure so the value is loaded before the branch, or check whether sub_080C31E8's 4th arg type affects literal placement.

Best score 300/44 insns (93.1%). Logic verified: arg0+0x28 is a u16 selector; r3 = D_080CEBB0 (a u16 table); switch(selector){case 0x2E:; case 0x2F: r3+=4; case 0x32: r3+=8; case 0x38: r3+=12; default: *(u8*)(*(void**)(arg1+0x28)+1) &= 0xFE;} then copy r3[0..3] to offsets +6,+8,+A,+C of *(arg1+0x28). First 32 of 44 instructions match exactly. Remaining diff: 3 missing `ldr r1,[r4,#0x28]` — the original re-loads arg1->+0x28 before stores 2,3,4 (does NOT keep it in a register), so the pointer is treated as volatile. agbcc caches the value for me no matter what I tried: plain void**, struct{...volatile void*}, volatile arg1 param, `*(volatile void**)` cast (with a qualifier-discard warning). Next agent: the pointer field at arg1+0x28 must be volatile AND the struct member must be read through a volatile-qualified lvalue that survives — try declaring arg1 as `volatile struct { u8 pad[0x28]; volatile void *p; } *` and accessing `arg1->p` four times, or cast arg1 to `volatile u8 *` and do `*(volatile u32*)((u8*)arg1+0x28)` each time.

Best score 1536/41 insns (62.5%). Logic verified: r5=arg0+0x38; sub_080144D8(arg0,r5); arg0+0x14 = 0x0866DCE4; idx=(s16)(arg0+0x22)+1; arg0+0x22=idx; (arg0+idx*2)[0x19]++; sub_080C31E0(arg0, *(void**)(arg0+0x14 + (*(u8*)(arg0+0x18+idx*2)<<2))); arg0+0x22=idx-1; sub_080144FC(arg0,r5). Remaining diff is register allocation: target uses push {r4,r5,lr} and keeps arg0 in r4, idx in r1 as a halfword via `movs r0,#0x22; ldrsh r1,[r4,r0]` (i.e. idx is a u16 loaded with ldrh then lsl #1); mine spills to r6 and emits lsls/lsrs #16 truncation on idx because I typed it s16. Tried s16/u16 idx, struct-typed arg0, int vs s16 idx*2. The target computes arg0+0x18+idx*2 as `adds r0,r4,#0; adds r0,#0x18; adds r0,r0,r1` (three adds) and loads the byte with `ldrb r0,[r0]` then `lsls r0,r0,#2` — so the shift is applied to the loaded byte, not the index. Next agent: type idx as u16, keep arg0 in a struct, and compute the byte index as `*(u8*)(arg0+0x18+idx*2) << 2` applied after the load.

Best attempt score 970/70 insns (86%). Structure is essentially right — verified against the byte-identical twin sub_08082FA0 (same 76 insns, same calls, same literals). Remaining diffs are regalloc + the D_02025FF0+0x18C2 access.

Key finding: the original loads 0x02025FF0 and 0x18C2 as TWO separate literals then adds (ldr r0,[pc]; ldr r1,[pc]; adds r0,r0,r1; ldrh r0,[r0]). My C folds the offset into the symbol address (single literal), which the linker rejects as "a pointer to D_02025FF0+0x18C2 where the original has 0x02025FF0". Tried: extern vu32 D_02025FF0 with &D_02025FF0+0x18C2, extern u8 D_02025FF0[] with D_02025FF0+0x18C2, extern u16 with &+0x18C2, and a struct { u8 _[0x18C2]; u16 w; } extern struct S D_02025FF0; — the struct got closest (1005) but still emitted two literals in the wrong order (0x02025FF0 then 0x18C2 became struct-base + field offset, regressed to 2 extra insns). The struct approach is the right direction: the field offset 0x18C2 is too big for an inline immediate so it must be a literal; the struct base is also a literal. Need the field to be declared so agbcc emits base-literal + offset-literal in that exact order. Also note 0x08671BB0 is a pointer table (words 0x03000001, 0x03000025) loaded via ldr r0,[pc]; ldr r2,[r0] — the original does NOT fold it either.

Other minor: target uses ldrsh r0,[r5,r2] (field_0x22 as s16 in r2) and keeps arg0 in r5, p in r4; my code spills differently. Suggest next agent try declaring D_02025FF0 as a struct with the 0x18C2 field named, or a global array symbol whose name the linker keeps separate from the offset.

BIG WIN for the codebase: to reproduce the target's two-literal form for `*(u16*)0x020278B2` (loads 0x02025FF0 and 0x18C2 as separate literals then adds), declare:
  struct S_02025FF0 { u8 _0x000[0x18C2]; u16 w; };
  extern struct S_02025FF0 D_02025FF0;
and access D_02025FF0.w. That made the linker happy and dropped the score from ~1400 to 325. Any agent hitting this pattern should use that struct.

Also: the final argument to sub_080C31E0 must be written as `(u32)p[idx*2] * 4 + arg0->field_0x14` (multiply-first, then add) — NOT `field_0x14 + (u32)p[idx*2]*4` — that ordering alone was worth ~680 score points.

To read the same global address both as u8 (ldrb+shifts) and as s8 (ldsb) without agbcc folding pointer+const into the literal pool: declare `extern union { u8 b[0x800]; s8 sb[0x800]; } D_020278D0;` and index the members (D.b[i] / D.sb[i]). Array indexing on an extern array NEVER folds the offset into the pooled literal; a pointer expression (D + 0x6A) DOES fold when that subexpression is CSE-shared (appears in 2+ addresses), which changes the pool bytes and shifts later pool slots (it even computed 0x6F as +5 from the folded D+0x6A). Also: pointer-add subexpressions used only ONCE are computed as adds from the pooled raw symbol register, not pooled — so keep shared offsets out of sibling address expressions.

KEY TOOLCHAIN FINDINGS (verified this session, apply project-wide):
1. CONST_INT pool literals (casts like (struct tbl*)0x080CF340) are lazily rematerialized by agbcc: the `ldr rx,[pc]` lands AFTER the index arithmetic (ldrb/lsls), right before the adds. The target instead loads the pool constant FIRST, then does ldrb/lsls. Declaring the data as a real extern symbol (SYMBOL_REF) flips this: `extern struct tbl D_080CF340[]; ... D_080CF340[idx].unk00` produces ldr-pool, ldrb, lsls, adds — exactly the target order. Symbols resolve correctly in this project (matched sub_0803C5F4 uses `extern u32 D_02027860;` + `&D_02027860` the same way). The "pointer to D_080CF340 where original has 0x4700BC01/0x802069A8" linker warnings when the function length mismatches are misalignment artifacts reading code bytes as data, NOT bad symbol resolution — ignore them if the ldr rows only differ in pc-offset.
2. To stop GCC folding small offsets into loads: the target forms p+4/p+8/q+1 as separate `adds` on the base pointer and loads with no offset (`ldr rX,[rY]`). Inline cast-struct expressions get reassociated ((p+idx*16)+4, folded into ldr [r,#4]). Pointer VARIABLES prevent this: `struct tbl *p4 = (struct tbl *)((u8 *)p + 4); ... p4[idx].unk00` gives adds rX,rP,#4 (imm3) + idx*16 + ldr [reg] ✓; p+8 target shape is copy (`adds r1,r7,#0`) then `adds r1,#8` (Thumb imm8 2-operand form needs rd=src).
3. Target register map (aim): ip=arg0 (mov ip,r0 first insn), r4=arg2, r5=arg1, r6=v, r7=p(base 0x080CF340); idx byte (arg2+4) loaded DIRECTLY into r2 (ldrb r2,[r4,#4]) in both branches and reused for b0 (lsls r1,r2,#1), reloaded 3x after (ldrb [r4,#4]) because b0 overwrote r2; q (0x080CF3A0) in r0 (adds r0,#1 reuses q's reg for q+1); b0→r2, b1→r3; p+4 via adds r0,r7,#4, p+8 via adds r1,r7,#0 + adds r1,#8, p+12 via adds r1,#4 reusing p+8's reg.
4. v/p shape that works: compute v with the symbol-indexed expression FIRST, then `p = D_080CF340;` AFTER → gives literal in temp reg + `adds r7,r1,#0` home copy at branch end (both branches, matching target exactly). Assigning p before v loads the literal straight into p's home (no temp) — wrong.

Plain `zero=0; *p=b|0x40` gave zero first (20); computing `v=b|0x40` before zero gave the OR too early (60). The fix is a comma expression that sequences the two constant assignments and the OR explicitly: `s32 v = (m = 0x40, zero = 0, b | m); *p = v;` with `s32 m;` declared at function scope. This emitted exactly `movs r0,#0x40; movs r2,#0; orrs r0,r1; strb r0,[r3]`. All the other findings in the older notes (switch dispatch, s32 val, raw 0x086426B4, volatile u8* p, named zero) remain necessary.

Pure pointer arithmetic `self + idx*2` (in either source operand order), s16/s32 temp, and a separate base pointer all stayed at 5. MATCHED (score 0). The 47-attempt wall was cracked with three combined levers:
(1) To stop agbcc reassociating `(base+C)+off` into `(base+off)+C` / `ldrb [r0,#C]`, assign `base+C` to a plain `int` temp FIRST, then index: `new_var = (u32)b1 + 1; *(u8*)(off + new_var)`. The copy makes GCC see `plus(pseudo, off)` with no foldable constant.
(2) REUSE THE SAME temp for the second load (`new_var = (u32)b2 + 2;`) via NESTED if blocks (`if (load1) { new_var=...; if (load2 && load3) ... }`), NOT separate temps — a second pseudo collapses the high-register prologue (score 1000). This keeps i in r2, p in r1, base in r4, base+3 in ip, arg0 in sb.
(3) Write `off + new_var` (offset FIRST), not `new_var + off` — this flips the final `adds r0, r0, r3` to the target's `adds r0, r3, r0` (2 regalloc rows, score 10 -> 0).

MATCHED (670 -> 620 -> 220 -> 60 -> 0 in 5 compiles). The structure was already there; these four source-level levers closed it, all worth knowing for other agbcc functions:

1) Remove the wrapper: `inline_fn(temp_r8)->f0` made agbcc emit an extra `mov r1,r8` + wrong load order. Writing `temp_r8->f4->f0` / `temp_r8->f4->f2` directly gives target's single `mov r2,r8` + two `ldr r0,[r2,#4]`.

2) Signed halving in one expression: `(s16)(((s32)(((s32)x) + (((u32)x) >> 31))) >> 1)` — the OUTER `(s32)` cast before `>>` is required; without it the sum is unsigned and agbcc emits `lsrs` instead of the target `asrs` (620 -> 220). Inline `((R4sub *)temp_r4->f20)->f8` twice in the expression so the destination `temp_r4->f4` is loaded before `s` (and CSE merges the two s loads into one ldrsh).

3) ADD OPERAND ORDER via INTEGER arithmetic: for `p = base + idx`, the C front end always canonicalises pointer+int to (plus (reg base) (reg idx)), which emits `adds rD, rBASE, rIDX` with dest = base. Target wants dest = idx (`adds r0, r0, r5`). Cast both sides to u32 and put idx first: `u8 *p = (u8 *)((u32)(arg0->f22 * 2) + (u32)arg0);`. Same trick fixed the final table lookup: `*((void **)(u8 *)((u32)off + (u32)arg0->f14))` (220 -> 60).

4) LOAD ORDER inside `ldrb; shift; ldr base`: target interleaves `ldrb r0,[r4]; ldr r1,[r5,#0x14]; lsls r0,r0,#2; adds r0,r0,r1`. Split the shift onto its own statement and put the base load between: `off = *new_var4; basev = (u32)arg0->f14; off <<= 2;` with a fresh `u32 basev` local declared at the end (a new high-numbered local used only in the last statement does not disturb earlier allocation): 60 -> 0.

Also: `r7->f24 = D_0866FAAC[temp_r6->f48]` inline (no idx local) loads the base literal before the index as target does; and for D_08671BB0 use `u32 *fp = D_08671BB0; ... *fp` so the base load is hoisted before the arg setup and the deref happens last.

2) Force repeated pointer reloads with `*(u8 *volatile *)(p48 + 0x54)` (volatile must qualify the POINTER, i.e. `u8 *volatile *`, not `volatile u8 **`). That emits `ldr r0,[r7,#0x54]` before each store instead of CSE-ing it.
3) Table literal: `u8 *tab = (u8 *)D_081021F4; t = (u32 *)(tab + 8);` gives `ldr r0,=base; adds r2,r0,#0; adds r2,#8` (a direct `D_081021F4+2` folds into one literal + one add and misses a row).

6) Keep `p18 = arg0 + 0x18` in a local so r4 holds it across the sub_080C31E4 call and is reused for the final index.
7) `|= 0x40` register swap (target `ldrb r1; movs r0,#0x40; orrs`): write it as `p2A = obj+0x2A; b = *p2A; flags = 0x40; flags |= b; *p2A = flags;` with `u8 b; u32 flags;`. MATCHED by opencode-deepseek-v4.1-flash-1 (150 -> 120 -> 0). Two levers finished it:
1) DIRECT GLOBAL-STRUCT FIELD ACCESS (already proposed #616): instead of caching D_02021E90 fields in u16 locals, write the tests directly as `D_02021E90.f146E & 0x302`, `D_02021E90.f146E & 1`, `D_02021E90.f146C & 4`, `D_02021E90.f146C & 8` through a global struct with named fields at 0x146C/0x146E. That took 150 -> 120 by making agbcc color the constant into r0 (dest) and the loaded value into r1/r3 exactly like the ROM, and removed all 6 regalloc rows. Caching f146E/f146C in locals (even if each used twice) does NOT give the target coloring.
2) s64 CONSTANT WORD ORDER (the last 4 reordered rows): the ROM's literal pool for the two 64-bit helper args stores 0x41F00000 then 0x00000000, and 0x3FE00000 then 0x00000000, and both `ldr r3,=0 / ldr r2,=0x41F0...` pairs match. Writing the natural constants `0x41F0000000000000ULL` / `0x3FE0000000000000ULL` makes agbcc pool the LOW word (0) first, giving [0,0x41F0] and shifting two 0x0000 nop halves early (4 `o` rows, score 120). Writing instead `0x0000000041F00000ULL` / `0x000000003FE00000ULL` (i.e. put the ROM's FIRST pool word in the LOW 32 bits, high word 0) emits the pool in the ROM's order and yields byte-identical code (score 0). So: agbcc stores a DImode constant's low 32 bits first in the constant pool — choose the 64-bit spelling so the intended first pool word is the low half.

WHAT IS NOW PROVEN (new this session, beats earlier guesses):
- The call is NOT a function-pointer/veneer call. Target `ldr r2,=0x08671BD8; ldr r3,[r2]; bl 0x08085600` is exactly `sub_080C31E8(arg0+0x18, arg0+0x22, 0, *(s32*)0x08671BD8)` (the harness maps symbol sub_080C31E8 to that site). The plain 4-arg call compiles byte-exact here; dropping the old `((Fn)*(void**)addr)(...)` hack fixed the extra `adds r4,r6,#0` and gave a clean 88-insn structure (score 330 vs 260 for the Fn hack, which the judge only scores better because of alignment noise).
- Literal placement: the pointer must be a raw cast taken at the point of use, `{ s32 *lit = (s32 *)0x08671BD8; sub_080C31E8(..., *lit); }` placed after the strb statement (inside the block, right before the call). That reproduces target's `ldr r2,[pc,#0x14]` after `strb` — the remaining `[pc,#0x10]` diff is only the 2-byte shift from the missing movs.
- DO NOT declare `extern s32 D_08671BD0/D_08671BD8`: the link resolves them to 0x0000E020 etc. and garbage results. Raw literal casts work and are not flagged by the linker.

ROOT CAUSE OF THE WALL (why no C spelling so far works): the cse pass runs record_jump_equiv across the extended basic block. The fallthrough of `bne` is the v==0 path, so cse records reg(v)==const0 and then substitutes the QImode constant 0 of the byte store with v's register. That extends v's live range across the bl to sub_08005820, so the allocator puts v in callee-saved r4 and the fresh `movs r1,#0` disappears (and with it the 2 bytes, cascading into every later beq/bne/bl offset and the `.byte 00 00` alignment pad). Target instead has v dead after `cmp` (in r0) and a fresh zero in r1.
Tried and NO EFFECT (byte-identical to plain `= 0`): named `u8 zero; zero = 0;` at the use point; `u8 zero = 0;` scoped in the block; `extern`-symbol literal; declaration orders. Volatile s16 compare only makes it worse (agbcc emits ldrh+lsls+asrs instead of ldrsh, substitution still happens). `s16 v = *(s16*)(r8+2); if (v == 0)` also byte-identical.

NEXT IDEA (untried, needs a compile): make the compare operand NOT a bare REG so record_jump_equiv bails: e.g. `s32 v = *(s16 *)(r8 + 2); if ((u16)v == 0)` (HImode subreg compare of an SImode reg), hoping the codegen stays `ldrsh r0,...; cmp r0,#0`. Risk: gcc may mask low half (extra insns). If that fails, this is a compiler-version wall (older agbcc cse did not substitute), not a C wall; suggest() would need an older agbcc variant, which the project does not have.

Residual target features (`last_diff` shows all rows):
1) f24 branch: target `ldrh r1,[r1,#0x28]; ldrh r0,[r0]; ands r0,r1` (f28 loaded first, AND dest = tbl value r0). Plain `f28 & tbl` gives ands r1,r0 (2 regalloc rows). With two branch-local u16 locals (v1/v2) the loads get hoisted and prologue still flips -> 935.
2) else branch: target `ldrh r2,[r0]` (mem value), `ldrh r0,[r1]` (tbl), `ands r0,r2`. Same color/dest problem.
3) zeros: target has `movs r4,#0; movs r3,#0` hoisted before `strh r0,[r2,#0xe]` (r4 later used for `strb`, r3 for `str [r5,#0x48]`). Splitting with a `u8 zz` gives 505 (zz takes r3 early, int zero still r1) — close but worse than 500, and it moves the 0x98*2 temp to r7. Note the target's r4-zero is only possible if the tbl pseudo is DEAD at that point, i.e. the dead store above is a reconstruction artifact of the permuter. So the real original must get tbl=r4 priority some other way (likely one more early reference to the table). Try: a 4th tbl use that emits no extra insn (e.g. an expression CSE folds), or keep the dead store and accept the zero mismatch.
4) tail: target `ldr r2,[pc,#0x1c]` (&D_08671BD0), `adds r1,r6,#0; adds r1,#0x22` computed inline; ours has the extra `adds r1,r4,#0` from the dead-store CSE and the literal in r1. Compile 3-4 confirm dropping the dead store costs the prologue.

ROM logic (derived instruction-by-instruction and confirmed by 8/8 matching prologue in one variant): struct {u32 type; s32 f4; s32 f8; u32 fC;}; a=arg0→r4, b=arg1→r1. `if (a->type<=1) return 1; if (b->type<=1) return 1; if (a->type==4 && b->type==4) return b->f4-a->f4; if (a->type==4) return a->f4==0?1:-1; if (b->type==4) return b->f4==0?-1:1; if (a->type==2 && b->type==2) return 0; if (a->type==2) return b->f4==0?-1:1; if (b->type==2) return a->f4==0?1:-1;` then `if (a->f4!=b->f4) return a->f4==0?1:-1; if (a->f8>b->f8) return a->f4==0?1:-1; if (a->f8<b->f8) return a->f4==0?-1:1; if (a->fC>b->fC) return a->f4==0?1:-1; if (a->fC<b->fC) return a->f4==0?-1:1; return 0;` (f8 signed: bgt/bge; fC unsigned: bhi/bcc; the tail blocks really test a->f4 against 0, NOT against b->f4). The ROM shares the a->f4 tails between the "a->type==4" and "b->type==2" paths, and the b->f4 tails between "b->type==4" and "a->type==2" — i.e. it does merge identical tails, keeping them INLINE just like the gcc that built the ROM.

8 compiles used; best 415 (96.9%, 136/137) reproduced 3x with the brief's source. The whole remaining gap is ONE compiler mechanism, now pinned down precisely: tail-merging of the two `f14 = 0` stores.

ROM tail: `if (ret>py) { fC+=py; if (f2&0x100) { movs r0,#0; str r0,[f14]; } b end; }` then `if (ret>0) { fC+=ret; f2|=4; movs r2,#0; b merge; }` / `else { f2|=4; movs r2,#0; }` / `merge: str r2,[f14]`. I.e. the two lower branches' identical store suffixes were merged into one, while the >py branch's own store (r0) stayed separate.
agbcc instead merges the WRONG pair: it gives the >py branch `movs r0,#0; b <shared>` and merges that store with the <=0 branch's (`str r2` at the tail of the >0 branch stays inline). So the branch displacements differ by 2 and the <=0 OR dest comes out `orrs r0,r1` instead of `orrs r1,r0`. Everything up to instruction 103 is byte-identical.

Variants tried this session, all worse: clean struct-typed rewrite with Obj{u16 f0,f2,f4,f6; s32 f8,fC,f10,f14} = 1655; `z=0`+`goto merge` (shared store) = 650 (fixes the >py branch's store but wrecks the >0 branch with an extra b before the orrs); `4 | f2` operand swap in the <=0 branch = 415 (no change); `z` shared in both lower branches with per-branch stores = 855 (agbcc hoists the duplicated `f2|=4` + store out of both branches); function-scope `zero` used in the >py store = 910 (merged with the final store); `else if` chain = 865. search_flags: -O2/-O3 = 415 (project flags best), -O1 = 1996, -Os = 2356.

MATCHED (score 0) after ~50 prior attempts had declared it a "regalloc/CSE wall" at 1160. Two source-shape discoveries, both essential:

1) The 6-byte stack buffer is a 2D array `u8 buf[3][2]` (ROM data 01 02 00 02 00 01 = pairs {1,2},{0,2},{0,1}), NOT `u8 buf[6]`. This is what produces the target's `ldrb r0,[r5,#0x1d]; ldrb r1,[r5,#0x1e]; ands r1,r0` operand order (the f1D/f1E/f1F check as `f1D[0] & f1D[1] & f1D[2]`) and the `(sp+1)+k2` address form for the second element vs the CSE'd `[r3,#1]` of the flat array. Using a flat `buf[k*2+1]` always floors.

2) The final selection block must be written as a short-circuit `&&` chain in this exact order:
   `if (fa == 0 && flags[buf[idx][1]] == 0) { *sel = buf[idx][rand&1]; } else if (fa != 0) { *sel = buf[idx][1]; } else { *sel = aa; }`
   with `u8 fa = flags[aa];` stored in a named local BEFORE `sel = (u8*)r5+0x20;` (this puts `adds r4,r1,#0` after the flags[aa] load, like the ROM). The nested `if/else` form is logically identical but emits the blocks in the wrong order (store-aa before the b-load/merged store), leaving 295. The && chain yields source block order S,R,T, matching the ROM's [random][b-addr][merged load+store][store aa] layout exactly.

Full matching source is preserved in the project as this function's entry.

MATCHED (score 0), 795 -> 530 -> 30 -> 20 -> 0. Prior agents called it a "terminal agbcc prologue wall" but the prologue was already right; the real bugs were source-shape:

1) The ROM has TWO copies of `sub_080C31E0(arg0, arg0->0x24)`: one at the early-return (which the `pr[4]==0` path falls through into) and one at the very end. Writing ONE shared `tail:` label (goto from both the early return and pr[4]==0 and the final path) gives score 530 with 3 instructions MISSING. Fix: write the call out at each return path:
   - early `if (sub_0806D450(...) > 0) { call(...); return; }`
   - `if (pr[4]==0) { sub_0808BB54(); call(...); return; }`
   - final `if (A==0x1C || (B==0 && C!=0)) call(...);`
   GCC cross-jumps the first two identical call+return blocks into the single mid-function copy, and keeps the final one separate, exactly like the ROM. Adding the second call also raises arg0's allocno priority, which fixes the 3-cycle register rotation (arg0 r5 / base r6 / hdr r7) -> all regalloc disappears (30 -> 20 only because of item 2). This also explains the "extra sb" ghosts: register pressure, not the prologue.

2) The timer block must be `r1 = 0x14 - cnt; r3 = r1 * 5 + 0x64;` (natural *5 synthesis: lsls+adds). Writing `r0 = r1*4 + r1;` swaps r0/r1 and leaves 4 regalloc rows (score 20). With `r1*5` it is an exact match.

3) Prune: the two `0x03000830` pointer writes each need their OWN scoped `u16 *p;` inside their `if` block (first -> r2, second -> r1). A single shared outer `p` makes both r2 (score 30).

MATCHED (score 0), 1150 -> 400 -> 0. Two levers broke the documented "zero-CSE / sb-coloring wall":

1) The ROM keeps 0x08634A4C in sb across calls and does `add r0, sb` with a separate 0xFFFFFE70 literal. A local `u32 r9 = 0x08634A4C;` gets constant-folded to 0x086348BC and rematerialized from the pool (no add, no sb). FIX (proposal #640/#641 style): declare `extern u8 D_08634A4C[];` and write the two stores as `*(u32*)(r8+0x24) = (u32)D_08634A4C;` and `*(u32*)(r8+0x24) = (u32)(D_08634A4C + 0xFFFFFE70);`. As an extern symbol the address cannot be folded with the offset, so agbcc emits `ldr r1,=D_08634A4C; mov sb,r1; str r1,[r0,#0x24]` and later `ldr r0,=0xFFFFFE70; add r0,sb` exactly like the ROM.

2) Zero handling: keep a single `u8 zero;` local. In the if branch assign `zero = 0;` only after `sub_08003A6C(...)` (so it materializes as `movs r4,#0` there and stays in r4 across the sub_08005E80 call); in the else branch assign `zero = (u8)(u32)r7;` (r7 is the NULL malloc result, so agbcc reuses r7 and emits no move, giving `strb r7,[...]`). This prevents the early `str r0,#0` stores from CSE-ing with the byte-store zero into sb, which was what clobbered the constant.

3) Literal-load placement: assign the callback pointers to locals at the right spot: `cbp = (u32*)0x08671BD0; base18 = r5 + 0x18; sub_080C31E8(base18, r5+0x22, 4, *cbp);` (and `cbp = (u32*)0x08671BB0; ...` in the else). That hoists `ldr r0,[pc]=...` before the base18 setup exactly like the ROM; passing `*(u32*)0x08671BD0` inline schedules the load late (score 400, the last 2 rows).

Prologue is `adds r0,r1,#4; mov ip,r0; ...; mov r6,ip`; then the *decrement* and the *tail call arg* use r6 (`ldr r0,[r6,#0x2C]`, `adds r1,r6,#0`), while the *reload* `if (count==0)` and the `sub_08003A6C` arg use r12 (`mov r0,r12; ldr r4,[r0,#0x2C]` ... `adds r0,#0x1C`). Root cause proven this session (important for the next agent):
- P (= *(a+0x6C), r4 in target) and copy (= P+4, r5 in target) are a genuine allocno tie.
- Writing the two stores as plain `*(s32*)(copy+0x60)=0` / `+0x54` gives the CORRECT encodings but SWAPS the two allocnos (P->r5, copy->r4; 35 regalloc rows, score 455).
- Writing them through single-use address temps (`r6n = r5+0x60; *r6n = 0;` and `int new_var2 = 0x54; *(s32*)(r5+new_var2)=0;`) restores the target coloring EXACTLY (P=r4, copy=r5, 0 regalloc rows) because the pre-allocation combine folds the temp's single-use def, moving 2 refs from the copy allocno to P — but the fold goes all the way through copy=P+4 and yields [r4,#0x64]/[r4,#0x58].
- Both temps are needed; either one alone does NOT flip the coloring (verified: r6n-only = 460, new_var2-only = 460).
- Adding harmless P refs elsewhere (temps for the >0x7C stores 0x128/0xC4, whose adds survive) does NOT flip it (verified: identical code to the plain version). So the lever is specifically REDUCING the copy's refs by 2 at alloc time, and every offset <=0x7C fold lands on the P base.

- The order is NOT scheduler-driven: agbcc emits these statements in source order. `zero = 0;` BEFORE the `|=` gives movs first (470); after gives it after strh (60). The ROM order therefore needs the OR result computed in one statement, `zero = 0` next, and the store third, i.e. a temp: `gfx = *(u16 *)obj | p25->f18C2; zero = 0; *(u16 *)obj = gfx;`. - But EVERY temp form then costs exactly the same 15 regalloc diffs (score 75): OR block becomes `ldr r3,[pc]; ldr r1,[pc]; adds r0,r3,r1; ldrh r1,[r7]; ldrh r0,[r0]; orrs r0,r1; movs r2,#0; mov sl,r2; strh r0,[r7]` (ROM: const in r0, addr in r1, obj value in r0, f18C2 in r1, scratch r1), plus in the cont block `mov r3,sl`/`mov r2,r8`/`movs r3,#8`/`movs r1,#0xa` where ROM has r2/r3/r1/r3. Confirmed 256 exactly with the stored source (reproduced this session: 256 = 11 regalloc + 1 missing + 1 stack + 1 extra). New diagnosis of what the whole residual really is, worth knowing: at 256 the LOOP already matches the ROM's `movs r2,#1` for the +0x4C byte (r2), and everything else in the body matches. So the two mutually exclusive requirements stand: (a) `one`'s pseudo must be created before `flags`'s for the AND to copy `one`, and (b) the `movs r7,#1` must be emitted after the flags load - and at -O1 with no scheduling pass the RTL order is the emitted order, so (a) implies the movs comes first.

(2) MY exact C (extern u16 D_080CE9C0/C8/D0/D8/E0 arrays, struct Hitbox, `u16 *boxParams = D_080CE9C0; switch (*(u16 *)(source+0x28)) { case 0: boxParams=D_080CE9E0; case 10: C8; case 13: D0; case 16: case 20: D8; }` then four stores through `*(struct Hitbox **)(target+0x28)`) reproduces the whole body, the jump table, the stubs and the stores — the ONLY difference is an added `push {lr}` + `pop {r0}` which shifts the table/literals by 4 (score 1936, and the strd/ldrd/cbz rows are the harness decoding the inline table data).
(3) The lr save is unconditional for branchy functions in this toolchain. Probed on THIS function, same flags: `if (a[0x28] & 1) *(u16*)(b+6) = 1;` -> `push {lr}` ... `pop {r0}; bx r0`; `switch (a[0x28]) { case 0: return 1; case 1: return 2; default: return 3; }` -> `push {lr}` ... `pop {r1}; bx r1`; a straight-line `*(u16*)a = *(u16*)b` is the only frameless shape. So no C with any control flow can be frameless here.
(4) Its two already-matched sibling templates prove the same source style is otherwise fine: sub_0802D678 (0x0802D678, matched) and sub_080216B0 (matched) have `push {r4,lr}` ... `pop {r4}; pop {r0}; bx r0` in the ROM, i.e. the ROM's compiler DOES save lr for these when a callee-saved register is in use. This one needs no callee-saved register and the ROM has no lr save, which is standard-correct leaf codegen but not reproducible here.

So: not matchable with this toolchain (either it is hand-written asm or it came from a different compiler build). Recommend setting aside as not_c; the same reasoning applies to every "frameless branchy leaf" in the remaining pool (dozens of them per prior notes) — those should be triaged the same way rather than retried 50-90 times each. Plain C body, correct and documented, is preserved above for whoever gets a toolchain that omits the lr save for leaves.

Residual diffs (only these two):
(a) `adds` encoding: ROM bytes at 0x080A2C62 are `41 18` = Rm field = r1 (=dest), Rn field = r0 (=base): operand order (base, index) with dest = index. agbcc emits the opposite field order. NEW this session: I proved the textual C operand order is irrelevant — `off = off + (s32)base2; tp = (s32 *)off;`, `off = (s32)base2 + off; tp = (s32 *)off;` and `tp = (s32 *)((u32)off + base2)` are ALL byte-identical 270. agbcc canonicalizes the plus so op1 is always the index pseudo, so the 3-operand encoding is forced; a 2-op/field-order variant needs a different expand path, which plain C (or an inline identity helper) evidently does not reach.
(b) the while-limit entry load `mov r0, sb; ldr r2, [r0, #0x5c]` must precede `mov r1, r8; movs r4, #0xa`; ours emits it after. Both compiles agree on this and both have the identical loop-bottom reload `mov r1, r9; ldr r0, [r1, #0x5c]`, so it is pure intra-block statement order.

3. VERIFIED LEVER: give the store's value a data dependency on the zero variable so the constant must be materialized before the store, using an operation that constant-folds away at -O2 so no extra instruction is emitted:

    s32 zero = 0;
    ...
    *((u16 *) r6) = tmp | zero;     /* NOT: *((u16*)r6) = tmp; */

agbcc keeps `(ior tmp zero)` until reload (zero is a REG with REG_EQUAL 0, so it is not folded by simplify_rtx), the zero is therefore materialized before the strh, in r0, exactly as the ROM has it — and the orrs never appears because reload folds the OR with the known-zero source. Score went 70 -> 0 in one compile. A volatile store (`*(volatile u16*)r6 = tmp`) also moves the zero before the store but adds `lsls/ lsrs #0x10` HImode normalisation (521), so prefer the `| zero` dependency. 6 compiles this session, best 20 (67/67 insns, only 4 regalloc rows at the two `& 0x8000` tests). Sharpest diagnosis yet of WHY #732 cannot be beaten from C here: in BOTH sites the loaded value (r2) is live ACROSS the AND (it is stored afterwards: `strh r2,[r1,#2]`), so both AND operands are live and gcc must copy one into the output pseudo; the ROM's gcc copies the MASK (`adds r0,r7,#0; ands r0,r2`) while this agbcc copies the VALUE (`adds r0,r2,#0; ands r0,r7`). Because 0x8000 is a compile-time constant, gcc's commutative canonicalisation always moves it to RTL operand 2, so the copy is always taken from operand 1 (the value). The only way to make the mask RTL operand 1 is to make it non-constant, which needs at least one instruction the ROM does not have. Measured this session: block-scoped `u32 mask = 0x8000;` with `mask & e0` = 20 (same 4 rows); function-scope mask + `u32 t = mask; t &= e0;` = 140 (mask materialisation hoisted to the function top, AND still value-first); `s32` value/comparison forms = 20; `static inline u32 andMask(u32 m,u32 b){m &= b; return m;}` with block-scoped mask = 20 (inlined and constant-folded back); `static inline u32 andM(u32 b){u32 m=0x8000; m&=b; return m;}` = 1322 (it DOES give mask-first `movs r0,#0x80; lsls r0,#8; ands r0,r2`, but the loss of the shared r7 re-colours the whole function: arg0 ip instead of r8, arg3 r7, prologue/epilogue change) - i.e. #878's lever fixes the AND orientation only by destroying the shared mask register that this ROM needs. 117 attempts / 8 models total. BEST 555 (98.1%, 298/298 insns), from 6622. The single biggest lever: replace the raw literal base `(struct Game*)0x02025368` with the DATA SYMBOL `extern u8 D_02025368[]; g = (struct Game*)D_02025368;`. That alone flipped the whole callee-saved allocation to the target's (arg0=sl/r10, base=sb/r9, hp/table=r8) and fixed the frame to sp-8. The earlier "global allocation wall" (6622) was really this: a SYMBOL_REF base is treated as a rematerializable address constant and loses the priority tie to the parameter, a raw integer literal wins it.

Second lever set (all needed to get from 2672 -> 835 -> 645 -> 555):
1. Correct struct: f2D6 is at 0x2D6 (the old best's struct put it at 0xD6!). Layout used: pad[0x8C], s16 f8C, pad2, u32 f90, pad[0x18], u16 fAC, pad[0x21A], s16 f2C8[4], s16 f2D0[3], s16 f2D6, pad[0x24], s16 f2FC, u32 f300, pad[8], u8 f30C[20].
2. Byte extraction of sub_0800FEF0's result must be three NAMED locals computed before the first call: `a=(v>>16)&0xFF; b=(v>>8)&0xFF; c=v&0xFF;` then FD54(a),FDC8(b,2),FDC8(c,2). Inline expressions make agbcc recompute after each call.
3. `t` is one variable reused (`t=D_080E0738[hp[0]-1]; if (t>0x05F5E0FF||t<*money) t=0; else t-=*money;`) and money must be `s32*` (signed -> bge, unsigned gives bhs).
4. The 0x2CA / 0x2D2 loads need a BLOCK-SCOPED pointer: `{ s16 *p=(s16*)((u8*)g+0x2C8); sub_0800FD54(p[1],...); }` -> gives movs #0xB2/lsls/add + movs #2/ldsh reg-offset. Writing g->f2C8[1] folds to the literal 0x2CA and loads it from the pool.
5. Loop: hoist `table = D_080CAFD0;` BEFORE the outer loop (it goes to r8 and forces p18/p22 to spill -> sp-8 frame), explicit walking pointer `tbl = table + k*2; ... *tbl ...; tbl++;` with `k = i*5;` named, and `j=0;` as a statement before k. Shape that scored best:
   i=0; p18=arg0+0x18; p22=arg0+0x22; table=D_080CAFD0;
   for (; i<=1; i++) { j=0; k=i*5; tbl=table+k*2; for (; j<=9; j++) { if (g->f30C[k*2+j]==0) sub_080063D4(0x086403A8,*tbl*32+0x06008000); tbl++; } }
   (i=0 as a separate statement BEFORE p18/p22 is load-bearing: folding it into the for-init cost 780.)
6. No `(double)` cast needed anymore.

MATCHED (score 0, 322 insns) this session, from a 6622 floor; the earlier note documents everything up to 555. Final deltas that took it 555 -> 115 -> 70 -> 30 -> 25 -> 20 -> 0:

1. Use a SEPARATE variable for the zero stored at the end instead of reusing the loop counter: `zero = 0; ... arg0[...] = zero;` (with `u32 zero;` declared). Reusing `j` for it cost 40 and kept j in the wrong register.

3. Table pointer: `tbl = (u16 *)(k * 4 + (u32)table);` — plain `table + k * 2` / `k * 2 + table` both make agbcc emit `adds r4,r1,r0` (table first); the u32 cast form gives the target's `adds r4,r0,r1`.
4. THE LAST WALL (2 rows, a swapped adjacent pair): target emits `lsls r0,r1,#2` (i*4) / `adds r7,r1,#1` (next) / `adds r6,r0,r1` (k). Writing `k = i*5; next = i+1;` gives k-then-next; `next` first gives next-then-k; `k = i*4; k += i;` breaks the regs. The winning shape splits the multiply into a named temp so the scheduler can interleave:
   `row = i * 4; next = i + 1; k = row + i;`  (with `u32 row;` declared)
   That reproduces lsls/next/adds exactly and the function went 20 -> 0.
5. Loop shell that kept i in r1: `i = 0;` as a statement before p18/p22/table, then `for (; i <= 1; i = next)` with `next` assigned in the body (this also produces the target's `adds r1,r7,#0` latch copy).

Critical: use ONE s32 local for both index and loaded value; write the -1 check as a plain early `return 0`; and the LAST bit-test as a TERNARY while earlier ones are `if`s. Having exactly two `return 0` statements makes agbcc emit `bne skip / movs r0,#0 / b end` for -1; three return-0 statements merge the blocks and flip the branch. A fully nested ternary duplicates blocks; three separate ifs return-0s merge wrong.
